explain.say: Think of a torch with two switches. Does it need both switches on, or just one? That tiny question is how computers think! The tiny parts that answer it are called logic gates. Look at the board: two gates side by side.

explain.say: Look at the left side, the AND gate. Picture two switches in a row on one wire. Electricity must pass both, so the bulb lights only when switch one AND switch two are on. If either is off, what happens to the bulb?

explain.say: Now meet NOT, the opposite gate: it turns a 1 into a 0 and a 0 into a 1. Watch the board sort which inputs light the bulb, written as 1, and which leave it dark, written as 0. Can you spot the AND that lights up?

groups.ask: What does a NOT gate do?

explain.say: Excellent thinking! Real gates are made of transistors, tiny switches with no moving parts, and a phone chip holds billions of them. Joined together, simple ANDs, ORs and NOTs add numbers, play music and run games. Challenge: which gate is a car alarm that rings if the door OR the window opens?

faq.a: An AND gate gives an output of 1, on, only when both inputs are 1. It is like two switches in a row: both must be on for the bulb to light.
asks: When is an AND gate on?

faq.a: An OR gate gives 1 when at least one input is 1. It is like two switches side by side: either one can light the bulb. It is 0 only when both inputs are 0.
asks: When is an OR gate off?

faq.q: What does a NOT gate do?
faq.a: A NOT gate has one input and flips it: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1. It is also called an inverter.
A truth table lists every possible input to a gate and the output for each. For an AND gate with two inputs there are four rows: 0 0, 0 1, 1 0 and 1 1, and only 1 1 gives 1.
asks: How do you read a truth table?

faq.q: What are logic gates made of?
faq.a: Modern logic gates are made from transistors, tiny electronic switches on a silicon chip. A few transistors make one gate, and a modern processor has billions of transistors.

facts: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all its inputs are 1; an OR gate outputs 0 only when all its inputs are 0.
George Boole described the algebra of true and false, now called Boolean logic, in 1854.

quiz.say: An AND gate gets the inputs 1 and 0. What is the output?
quiz.why: AND needs both inputs to be 1, so one 0 makes the output 0.

wrong.1: That would be OR, which needs only one input to be 1.
wrong.2: Logic gates only output 0 or 1, never 2.

quiz.say: A lamp should turn on if the front door OR the back door opens. Which gate fits?
quiz.show: Either door turns on the lamp: which gate?
quiz.why: OR gives 1 when at least one input is 1, so either door is enough.

wrong.0: AND would need both doors open at once.
wrong.2: NOT has one input and just flips it.
